pr_title: Add support for caching solutions. Remove GEMRC modifications.
pr_body:
This pull request adds an enhancement to the internal Bundler class
to cache solution sets. This prevents Vagrant from generating a
solution for configured plugins on every run. Modifications to
the configured plugin list (global or local) will result in the
cached solution being invalidatd and resolved again.

Initially reported in #11142, reproduction was difficult until
adding the `aws-sdk` which include a large number of dependencies.

Timing for initial run without solution set:

```
$ time vagrant
...
real    0m12.213s
user    0m11.285s
sys     0m0.617s
```

Timing for run with solution set:

```
$ time vagrant
...
real    0m2.483s
user    0m1.730s
sys     0m0.622s
```

Also included is the removal of the GEMRC modifications required
for Windows (won't be required for next release due to Ruby version upgrade).

Fixes #11142 #11315

issue_context.title: Vagrant Commands Slow to Start (Due to `Generating new plugin set instance. Skip gems - []`)
issue_context.body:
### Vagrant version

Vagrant 2.2.5

### Host operating system

Mac OSX Mojave

### Guest operating system

Irrelevant

### Vagrantfile

Irrelevant

### Debug output

Note that I have turned on timestamps for all of the stdout/stderr lines.

https://gist.github.com/jamiejackson/9dd3e99868766d06af47b965717f8c2b

### Expected behavior

Vagrant commands should execute quickly, say, in within a second.

### Actual behavior

Vagrant commands take at least 15 seconds to initialize.

I realize I have a gem that has lots of dependencies, but I think that whatever Vagrant's doing, that it should be faster or should have a way to be bypassed during normal operation.

### Steps to reproduce

Have plugins installed. Run any vagrant command (e.g., `vagrant help`). You don't even have to be in a project directory.
